# 1g: web UI

## Read first

- [ui/design/README.md](../ui/design/README.md), then `tokens.css`, `components.css` and the screens in `ui/design/screens/`.
- [ui/design-brief.md](../ui/design-brief.md), with its list of what is not designed yet, and [architecture.md](../architecture.md) sections HTTP API and Events.
- The As built sections of [1b](1b.md), [1d](1d.md), [1e](1e.md) and [1f](1f.md).

## Done when

- The Vue app implements every screen in the design, in both themes and at phone width, with live updates.
- `make web-check` passes.
- A local run with `SHELF_DEV_FAKE_SOURCE=true` passes the UI part of the checklist below.
- The browser console shows no CSP violations on any screen.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stack | Vue 3 with `<script setup>`, Vite, TypeScript, Vue Router, Pinia, Vitest and `@vue/test-utils`. No component library. | The design defines the components. |
| Styles | `tokens.css` from the design as the base. Each component gets a scoped stylesheet built from its rules in `components.css`. No inline `style` attributes in templates; dynamic values, such as a knob's angle, go through CSS variables set from script. | The strict CSP. |
| Fonts | Self-hosted files under `web/public/fonts`: IBM Plex Sans, IBM Plex Sans Condensed, IBM Plex Mono and Pixelify Sans, all under the SIL Open Font License. | `font-src 'self'`. |
| Icons | The icons draw the header's three-bar meter. `web/public` holds `favicon.svg`, `favicon.ico`, `apple-touch-icon.png`, Safari's `safari-pinned-tab.svg` and `manifest.webmanifest`. The manifest lists maskable 192 and 512 PNGs, so a phone can add shelf to its home screen. `make icons` renders the PNGs and the ICO from `favicon.svg` and the full-bleed `web/icons/icon.svg`. | All are same-origin files, which the CSP allows. |
| Routes | `/search`, `/downloads`, `/downloads/:id`, `/status`. `/` redirects to `/search`. | The shell's sections. |
| Stores | `sources` holds capabilities, formats and health. `search` holds the query, the sources that are on, the type and pages per source. `downloads` holds lists and details. `events` owns the `EventSource`. | Small, separate state. |
| Live updates | One `EventSource` on `/api/events`. On reconnect the stores reload what they show. A download panel opens its own log stream. | architecture.md: the stream has no replay. |
| Search across sources | The store sends one `/api/search` per source that is on. The answers merge by rank: each source's first item, then each source's second, and so on. Load more asks every source for its next page. A source that fails shows its error, and the other source's results stay. | `/api/search` searches one source, and the design shows one list. |
| Links in the search field | A value that parses as a Qobuz or Apple Music URL calls `/api/resolve` instead of searching. `/search?q=<value>` fills the field and runs it. | The brief. The bot's artist confirmation links to `/search?q=<link>`. |
| Covers | Apple artwork templates get the size the cell shows, times the device pixel ratio. Qobuz covers use the sizes the API offers. | Sharp covers without large files. |
| Keyboard | Tables keep a row cursor: arrow keys move it, Enter opens the panel, Escape closes it, and `/` moves focus to the search field. | The brief's keyboard rule and the design. |
| Theme | Night is the default; the switch in the shell saves the choice in `localStorage`. Replaces "follows the system". | The design is phone first and dark first. |
| Phone layout | The phone layout applies below 720px of width, through a media query that carries the design's `ph` rules. | The canvas draws only 390px and 1440px frames. Check the width on a real phone and a tablet. |

## Pages

| Route | Design screens | API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/search`, `/search?q=` | `MS-phone-start`, `MS-phone-search*`, `MS-phone-album*`, `MS-phone-artist`, `MS-phone-playlist`, `MS-phone-link`, `MS-phone-first-run`, `MS-desk-search*`, `MS-desk-album`, `MS-desk-artist`, `MS-desk-playlist`, `MS-desk-link`, `MS-states` | `/api/sources`, `/api/search`, `/api/resolve`, `/api/items`, `POST /api/downloads` |
| `/downloads`, `/downloads/:id` | `MS-phone-downloads`, `MS-phone-downloads-empty`, `MS-phone-download`, `MS-desk-downloads` | `/api/downloads`, `/api/downloads/{id}`, `/log`, `/cancel`, `/retry`, `/api/library/scan` |
| `/status` | `MS-phone-status`, `MS-phone-signin*`, `MS-desk-status` | `/api/sources`, `/api/applemusic/wrapper/*`, `/api/library/scan`, `/api/telegram` |

## As built

Finished on 2026-11-04. `make check`, `make lint`, `make web-check` and `docker build .` pass. Vitest has 130 tests in 15 files, and each checklist line has its test under the name given there.

The manual lines ran in headless Chrome against the real binary with the fake source, on fresh data, at 390 and 1440 pixels and in both themes. Downloads, the Queued slot, Retry, the log stream, Download all, the row cursor and the keys ran for real. The fake source's slowest album takes 0.6 seconds, so the running and queued screens ran with stubbed lists. No wrapper runs in that setup, so sign-in and the rate-limit wait ran with stubbed answers. The console showed no CSP violation on any screen. Seven widths from 320 to 1920 pixels show no sideways scroll and no control past the edge.

Not yet tried: a real phone and tablet, real Qobuz and Apple covers in the browser, and sign-in against a real wrapper. Checks in [manual-checklist.md](../manual-checklist.md) cover them in 1h.

What differs from the contract:

- Styles: parts that one component owns are in its scoped style. Parts that many share, such as `.key`, `.win`, `.row` and `.lcd`, are in `web/src/styles/parts.css`, generated once from `components.css`, because a scoped copy of each would repeat them in most components. `layout.css` replaces the screens' inline styles.
- Phone layout: CSS uses the media query, and `usePhone` follows the same query, because the phone and desktop templates differ. 720 pixels holds up. Between 720 and about 950 the grids drop columns, and the menubar wraps.
- Grids: the results use the panel's narrow grid when they have less than 900 pixels, which a `ResizeObserver` measures. The history drops Source, Kind, Took and Size in a container query, and the download panel still shows them.
- Routes: an open panel is `?open=source:kind:id` and the sign-in is `?signin=1`, so a phone's back button closes them. `?type=` keeps the result type.
- Stores: `status` holds the scan, the bot and the wrapper, and `theme` the theme, beside the contract's four.
- Links: any `http` or `https` link goes to `/api/resolve`, not only Qobuz and Apple Music links, so shelf's own answer shows and fake links work.
- Theme: the phone has no menubar, so its switch is on Status.
- Sign-in: Send a new code stops the sign-in and returns to the first step, because the wrapper can't send a code again. Close during a sign-in stops it too.
- Track lamps in compact views show the counts in order, since events carry no per-track state. The download panel lists each track's real state.
- A running track says Downloading, not a percentage, because the API has no per-track progress.

Backend changes for the UI:

- `/api/search` and `/api/items` answer 429 with "<source> is slowing us down, try again in a minute" for `source.ErrRateLimited`, which Apple Music wraps. The answer was a generic 502 before.
- Downloads answer `origin_user`, the Telegram user's name, for "who asked".
- The fake source's covers are data URLs, because `fake.test` broke the CSP.
- The supervisor keeps Apple's `server message` when an `auth error` line follows it.

Left out, because no API has the data:

- The Rate limits module of Status. Nothing reports a limit before a search hits it.
- "Last request" and "401 at 14:05" on the Qobuz card.
- The rate-limit wait for Qobuz. `qobuz-dl-go` doesn't tell a 429 from other errors, so it answers the generic 502. The wait counts down a fixed minute, since the API has no exact time.
- A playlist's description. `source.Item` has no such field.

Of the brief's list of what is not designed: Compilations and Appears on, and an artist row that opens into its albums, are built. The row opens on the desktop, and the phone shows the albums in the download panel.

Notices when a download ends are a setting on Status, kept per browser in `localStorage` as `shelf.notices`:

| Level | Shows |
| --- | --- |
| Off | Nothing when a download ends |
| Failures, the default | Failed and Done with errors |
| All | Those, and Downloaded |

A notice covers every top-level download that ends while the page is open, whoever asked, including the bot's. A canceled or skipped download and an album of an artist show none, and neither do ended downloads in a list the page reads. A problem stays until dismissed, and the rest go after 8 seconds. The setting doesn't touch Queued or a refused request, and the bot's messages don't change. The phone shows notices in its slot on Search, Downloads and Status. The desktop has a slot at the top of the side column, or of the page on Status, for notices with a lamp, so Queued stays out of it as the design says. A refused download showed nothing on the desktop before this slot.

Row density is a second setting on Status, on the desktop only, kept per browser in `localStorage` as `shelf.density`. Comfortable is the default. Compact puts the class `compact` on the root: rows are 40px, track rows 36px and covers 30px, in the results, the panels' lists and History. The switch has a preview of two made-up History rows that can't be clicked. The phone has no switch and ignores the setting.

Bugs that testing found and this step fixed:

- A page kept for the back button held its event stream, so the seventh load of a tab hung on the browser's six connections. The stream now closes on `pagehide`.
- The sign-in dialog lost a failed sign-in's message when the wrapper moved on.
- Opening `/status` directly never read the wrapper, because the check asked before the sources had loaded.
- The design's red on a module is about 2:1, below AA. Error text is now a pale red at night and a dark red by day, at 4.7:1 or better.

Notes for 1h:

- Check the sign-in dialog and the covers on the real deployment, with a phone and a tablet.
- A local run inherits `SHELF_QOBUZ_TOKEN` from the shell. Unset it for a run that should use only the fake source, or that run logs in to the real account.
